ringcask

Allocation-free ring buffers for real-time Rust. Once a buffer is created, pushing and popping never touch the allocator, never lock, and never panic, so the crate is safe to use inside audio callbacks and interrupt handlers.

The API is deliberately small. There is one type, RingBuffer, with a handful of methods, and a no_std feature for embedded targets that provide their own allocator for the initial construction.

Example

let mut rb = RingBuffer::with_capacity(1024);
rb.push(sample)?;

Status

The crate is used in production by two audio plugins, but the API may still change before 1.0.

Benchmarks, design notes, and the changelog are in the docs folder. Documentation for the latest release is on docs.rs.
